header.userPrompt:
Add a `--keep-changes` CLI flag to the flow runtime and the orca shell, letting a fresh run keep uncommitted working-tree changes instead of stashing them.

Background: today `FlowLifecycle.applyCleanlinessPolicy` (runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/FlowLifecycle.scala) auto-stashes a dirty tree in every case except a fresh `--skip-branch` run, which tolerates it (files stay in place and are swept into the first stage's commit). Branch handling and dirty-tree handling are two independent decisions; this flag makes the dirty-tree one independently selectable, serving the "hand-written spec file in the tree, let orca create the branch" use case.

Requirements:

1. New flag `keepChanges: Flag` in `OrcaArgs` (runner/src/main/scala/orca/OrcaArgs.scala), CLI name `--keep-changes`, doc: keep uncommitted/untracked files in the working tree instead of stashing them (fresh runs only).

2. Cleanliness policy in `FlowLifecycle.applyCleanlinessPolicy`:
   - FRESH run + `--keep-changes`: tolerate the dirty tree in BOTH modes (normal branch-creating and `--skip-branch`): no stash, emit the same informational Step the fresh skip-branch path uses ("leaving N uncommitted/untracked file(s) in place for the flow"), return `UntrackedFiles.Keep`. In normal mode the kept files survive branch creation (`git checkout -b` keeps the working tree) and are swept into the first stage's commit — state this in the scaladoc.
   - RESUME: always auto-stash, even with the flag; emit one Step noting `--keep-changes` is ignored on resume. Rationale (already documented for skip-branch): an interrupted stage's uncommitted partial work must not leak into the re-run.
   - Fresh `--skip-branch` behavior without the flag is unchanged (still tolerates).

3. Interactive choice: on a FRESH run with a dirty tree, when `--keep-changes` was NOT passed and stdin is a real terminal, ask the user before deciding: stash (default) / keep for the flow / abort. Abort raises `OrcaFlowException` before any tree mutation. Do NOT ask when off-tty, or when the decision is already made (`--keep-changes` → keep; fresh `--skip-branch` → keep, as today). Headless default stays stash, so existing non-interactive behavior is byte-for-byte unchanged. Follow the repo's existing tty-gating conventions (prompts must never run off-tty). Keep the prompt minimal — a numbered stderr menu read from stdin is fine; no new UI infrastructure.

4. Shell plumbing: `orca run` gains `--keep-changes`, passed through to the flow child alongside `--skip-branch` (shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/cli/Cli.scala and RunCli.scala, shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/run/FlowFlags + FlowLauncher, shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/actions/RunAction.scala). Update the shell help text.

5. Docs: document `--keep-changes` wherever `--skip-branch` is documented (README), and amend the flow-lifecycle section of adr/0018-stage-bound-flow-runtime.md (§2.5 cleanliness) with the new flag and the resume rule. Mention the sharp edge, which already exists for skip-branch: kept tracked modifications are unprotected until the first stage commit — a failure before that point runs `git reset --hard` and destroys them (untracked files survive). Documented, deliberately not mitigated.

6. Tests: unit tests for the policy matrix in the runner test suite (fresh/resume x normal/skip-branch x flag on/off), plus the interactive decision logic factored so it is testable without a real terminal (inject the tty probe and the prompt function, the way `RunCli.readTask` injects `tty`/`readStdin`). No integration tests.

Constraints: zero compiler warnings; run scalafmt before committing; follow existing code and comment conventions.

resultJson.description:
Add a `--keep-changes` flag to the flow runtime and plumb it through the orca shell's `orca run`, so a fresh run can keep uncommitted/untracked working-tree changes instead of auto-stashing them. Today only a fresh `--skip-branch` run tolerates a dirty tree; branch handling and dirty-tree handling are independent decisions, and this flag makes the dirty-tree one selectable on its own — serving the "hand-written spec file in the tree, let orca create the branch" hand-off use case. Kept files survive branch creation (`git checkout -b` keeps the working tree) and are swept into the first stage's commit.

On resume the flag is always ignored (auto-stash, with an informational Step), because an interrupted stage's uncommitted partial work must not leak into the re-run — the same rationale already documented for skip-branch. Additionally, a fresh run with a dirty tree and no flag now asks the user on a real terminal (stash default / keep / abort), gated by the repo's existing tty conventions so headless behavior stays byte-for-byte unchanged. The sharp edge — kept tracked modifications are unprotected until the first stage commit, since a failure before that runs `git reset --hard` — already exists for skip-branch and is documented, deliberately not mitigated.

tasks.title: Runner: add --keep-changes to OrcaArgs and extend the cleanliness policy (headless matrix)
tasks.description: Add `keepChanges: Flag = Flag()` to `OrcaArgs` (runner/src/main/scala/orca/OrcaArgs.scala) with doc "keep uncommitted/untracked files in the working tree instead of stashing them (fresh runs only)" — mainargs' kebab mapping yields `--keep-changes`. Rework `SetupSession.applyCleanlinessPolicy` in runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/FlowLifecycle.scala so the fresh-vs-resume peek (`store.loadDetailed()` pre-stash, gating only) runs in BOTH modes: FRESH + (`--skip-branch` OR `--keep-changes`) → tolerate the dirty tree (no stash, the existing "leaving N uncommitted/untracked file(s) in place for the flow" Step, return `UntrackedFiles.Keep`); RESUME → always `ensureClean` + `Remove`, emitting one Step that `--keep-changes` is ignored on resume (interrupted stage's partial work must not leak into the re-run) when the flag was passed; FRESH normal mode without the flag → stash exactly as today. Update the load-bearing scaladocs: `setup`'s cleanliness paragraph (currently claims only skip-branch peeks), `applyCleanlinessPolicy`, and `FlowSetup.untrackedOnFailure` (Keep is no longer skip-branch-only); state in the scaladoc that in normal mode kept files survive branch creation (`git checkout -b` keeps the working tree) and are swept into the first stage's commit. Tests in runner/src/test/scala/orca/runner/FlowLifecycleTest.scala covering the fresh/resume × normal/skip-branch × flag on/off matrix — mirror the existing skip-branch dirty-tree tests (~lines 2172–2390): normal-mode fresh + flag keeps a modified tracked file and an untracked file through to the first stage commit with zero stash entries; resume + flag still stashes and emits the ignored-flag Step; unflagged cells byte-identical to today. Zero warnings; scalafmt.

tasks.title: Runner: interactive stash/keep/abort prompt on fresh dirty-tree runs, factored for testability
tasks.description: In FlowLifecycle, factor the dirty-tree decision into a testable unit: a small choice enum (stash/keep/abort) and a decision function taking the run facts (isResume, skipBranch flag, keepChanges flag, dirty count) plus an injected `tty: Boolean` and `ask: () => Choice` — the `RunCli.readTask(task, tty, readStdin)` injection pattern. Ask ONLY when fresh + dirty + no `--keep-changes` + not `--skip-branch` + tty; every other case is already decided (flag/skip-branch → keep, resume → stash, off-tty → stash default, byte-for-byte unchanged headless). Production prompt: minimal numbered menu on stderr, one stdin line, stash on empty/unrecognized input, no new UI infrastructure (no jline in runner); production tty probe `TtyProbe.stdin()` (tools/src/main/scala/orca/subprocess/TtyProbe.scala, private[orca], visible to runner). Abort throws `OrcaFlowException` from `applyCleanlinessPolicy`, i.e. before any stash or branch mutation. Thread the probe and prompt through `setup`/`SetupSession` as defaulted parameters so `runFlow` is untouched. Unit tests without a real terminal: off-tty never invokes `ask`; already-decided cases never invoke `ask`; ask→keep returns Keep and emits the informational Step; ask→stash stashes; ask→abort raises `OrcaFlowException` with the tree untouched. Zero warnings; scalafmt.

resultJson.brief:
## Project

Scala 3 sbt multi-module build (direct-style Scala + Ox). Before touching any Scala code, load the `direct-style-scala` skill (mandated by CLAUDE.md, applies to subagents too). Build/test: `sbt compile`, `sbt test`, `sbt "runner/test"`, `sbt "shell/test"`, `sbt scalafmtAll` before committing. Zero compiler warnings required. Tests are munit (`munit.FunSuite`). Never commit unless asked; never add Claude as co-author.

## Modules and files

- **runner** — the flow runtime.
  - `runner/src/main/scala/orca/OrcaArgs.scala` — `case class OrcaArgs(userPrompt: String, verbose: Flag, skipBranch: Flag)` parsed with mainargs `ParserForClass`. mainargs' default kebab mapping turns `skipBranch` into `--skip-branch`, so a `keepChanges: Flag = Flag()` field with an `@arg(doc = ...)` yields `--keep-changes` with no extra config.
  - `runner/src/main/scala/orca/runner/FlowLifecycle.scala` — the heart of the change. `setup(...)` (line ~291) is `private[orca]`, called from `runFlow`; it runs `abortIfNoCommits`, `abortIfBranchBusy`, `snapshotLog`, then `SetupSession.applyCleanlinessPolicy()` (line ~490), then `restoreLogIfMissing`, settings discovery, `bindBranch`. `SetupSession` is a private class bundling `args/agent/git/workDir/.../emit`. Current policy logic: `if args.skipBranch.value` → peek `store.loadDetailed().isInstanceOf[LoadResult.Loaded]` (isResume); resume → `git.ensureClean("orca: starting flow")` + return `UntrackedFiles.Remove`; fresh → if `git.dirtyPaths()` non-empty, emit `OrcaEvent.Step(s"leaving ${dirty.size} uncommitted/untracked file(s) in place for the flow")` and return `UntrackedFiles.Keep`; else `Remove`. Normal mode: unconditional `ensureClean` + `Remove`. **Key change:** normal mode must now also peek fresh-vs-resume pre-stash. `setup`'s scaladoc (the long "Cleanliness policy (ADR 0018 amendment)" paragraph) explicitly says "only skip-branch mode peeks" — that claim must be amended, along with `applyCleanlinessPolicy`'s and `FlowSetup.untrackedOnFailure`'s docs ("Keep only when... fresh skip-branch mode" is no longer the only case). The peek is a throwaway read gating only the stash decision, never the fresh-vs-resume routing — the authoritative `store.loadDetailed()` stays in `bindBranch`, post-stash; preserve that invariant and its doc.
  - `runner/src/test/scala/orca/runner/FlowLifecycleTest.scala` — munit suite; each test uses `orca.testkit.GitRepo.seeded()` (real temp git repo), `OsGitTool`, `StubAgent.claude`, `TerminalInteraction.start(out = PrintStream(ByteArrayOutputStream()), useColor = false, animated = false)` inside `ox.supervised`, and the exit-free `runFlow(...)` seam (or `flow(...)`) with `stackSettings = Some(StackSettings.empty)`, `workDir`, and a listener to capture `OrcaEvent.Step`s. The skip-branch dirty-tree tests at lines ~1998, ~2172, ~2238, ~2301, ~2338 are the exact patterns to mirror for the new matrix cells (they assert on `git.dirtyPaths()`, `git stash list` emptiness, and file content sweeping into the stage commit). `OrcaArgs(prompt, skipBranch = Flag(true))` is how flags are passed (`mainargs.Flag` imported).
- **tools** — shared tooling, runner depends on it.
  - `tools/src/main/scala/orca/tools/GitTool.scala` — `enum UntrackedFiles { Remove, Keep }`; `def ensureClean(stashMessage: String)(using WorkspaceWrite): Unit` (stashes with `-u` iff `dirtyPaths()` non-empty, emits its own Step with the `git stash pop` hint); `def dirtyPaths(): List[String]` (porcelain lines, read-only); `def discardUncommitted(untracked: UntrackedFiles)` (always `reset --hard`; `Keep` skips the `clean -fd` — hence kept TRACKED modifications die on failure teardown, untracked survive: the documented sharp edge).
  - `tools/src/main/scala/orca/subprocess/TtyProbe.scala` — `private[orca] object TtyProbe`, `def stdin(): Boolean` / `def stdout(): Boolean` (shells out to `test -t`). Accessible from `orca.runner`. This is the production tty probe to inject.
- **shell** — the interactive shell + CLI.
  - `shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/run/FlowLauncher.scala` — `case class FlowFlags(verbose: Boolean, skipBranch: Boolean)` (line 29; no defaults, deliberately — the scaladoc explains it exists to prevent transposed positional Booleans; a third `keepChanges: Boolean` follows the same style). `def argv(...)` (line 76) appends `Seq("--", task) ++ verboseArgs ++ skipBranchArgs` — the flow's own flags go AFTER `--`, spelled exactly as `OrcaArgs` parses them; add `--keep-changes` there and to the scaladoc listing the argv shape.
  - `shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/cli/Cli.scala` — `@main def run(...)` (line 144) has `skipBranch: Flag` with `@arg(doc = ...)`; add `keepChanges: Flag` with a matching doc (this IS the shell help text — `commandHelp` renders it) and pass through to `RunCli.run`.
  - `shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/cli/RunCli.scala` — `def run(flowRef, task, verbose, skipBranch, honorPin, workDir, tty)` builds BOTH `FlowFlags(verbose, skipBranch)` (honor-pin path) and `RunAction.RunOptions(verbose, skipBranch, fallback)` — thread `keepChanges` through both. Its `readTask(task, tty, readStdin)` is the repo's canonical injected-tty/injected-read testable pattern to imitate in the runner.
  - `shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/actions/RunAction.scala` — `case class RunOptions(verbose: Boolean, skipBranch: Boolean = false, fallback: FallbackPolicy)`; give the new field a `= false` default so `Main.scala`'s two `RunOptions(...)` call sites (interactive menu line ~364, resume line ~400) compile unchanged; `run` builds `FlowFlags(opts.verbose, opts.skipBranch)` — extend.
  - `shell/src/main/scala/orca/shell/actions/AuthorAction.scala:155` — constructs `FlowFlags(verbose = false, skipBranch = false)`; must gain `keepChanges = false`.
  - Tests: `shell/src/test/scala/orca/shell/run/FlowLauncherTest.scala` (argv-shape tests, e.g. "argv adds --skip-branch ... after -- when set", asserts ordering via `indexOf`), `shell/src/test/scala/orca/shell/cli/CliTest.scala:45` ("run: --skip-branch parses too (fails later, at flow resolution)"), `shell/src/test/scala/orca/shell/actions/AuthorActionTest.scala:134` (asserts the recorded `FlowFlags`).

## Interactive prompt design constraints

- Ask ONLY when: fresh run + dirty tree + `--keep-changes` NOT passed + NOT `--skip-branch` (skip-branch fresh already means keep) + stdin is a real tty. Everything else keeps today's behavior exactly (headless default = stash). Repo convention (ADR 0021 §4, `Cli.requireTty`, `RunCli.readTask`): prompts must never run off-tty; tty is always an injected Boolean/thunk (production: `TtyProbe.stdin()`), never probed inside the decision logic.
- Keep it minimal: numbered menu on stderr (`Console.err`), one line read from stdin (`scala.io.StdIn.readLine` or `System.in`), stash on empty/unrecognized input (stash is the default). No jline/ShellUi in the runner — the runner has no UI infrastructure and must not gain one.
- Abort throws `OrcaFlowException` (in package `orca`, runner module — already imported in FlowLifecycle) BEFORE any tree mutation; `applyCleanlinessPolicy` runs before any stash/branch mutation, so raising there satisfies this. `abortIfBranchBusy` shows the message-style convention (lowercase, names the ways out).
- Testability: factor a pure decision (e.g. an enum Stash/Keep/Abort and a function taking `isResume`, `skipBranch`, `keepChanges`, `dirtyCount`, `tty: Boolean`, `ask: () => Choice`) so unit tests inject `tty` and a recording `ask` — exactly the `RunCli.readTask(task, tty, readStdin)` shape. Thread the probe/prompt into `setup` (or `SetupSession`) as defaulted parameters so `runFlow` needs no change.

## Event/message conventions

`OrcaEvent.Step` messages are lowercase, informational, self-contained (see the existing "leaving N uncommitted/untracked file(s) in place for the flow" — reuse this exact string for the keep path in both modes). Resume-with-flag needs one Step noting `--keep-changes` is ignored on resume (say why in the same breath, matching existing Step style). `emit` is available inside `SetupSession`.

## Docs

- `README.md`: line ~63 "Useful flag: `--skip-branch` ..." one-liner list; lines ~311–341 the flow-lifecycle bullets (**Start** bullet documents skip-branch dirty-tree tolerance — add `--keep-changes` alongside, including the resume rule; **Failure teardown** bullet documents the `UntrackedFiles.Keep` consequence — extend with the normal-mode kept case and the reset --hard sharp edge on tracked modifications); line ~913 the CLI table row for `orca run` key flags. User's style rules: maximally short, simple language.
- `adr/0018-stage-bound-flow-runtime.md` §2.5: amendments are blockquotes `> **Amendment (YYYY-MM-DD).** ...` attached to the requirement they modify. Skip-branch's dirty-tree tolerance lives in R2's 2026-07-25 amendment (lines ~378–414); the stash rule is R4 (line ~422); failure teardown is R5 (~424–442, already explains the skip-branch Keep case). Add a new dated amendment (today: 2026-08-25) under R4 covering: the flag, keep-in-both-modes on fresh, the interactive ask (tty-gated, stash default, abort option), the resume-ignores rule, and the unprotected-until-first-commit sharp edge (documented, deliberately not mitigated).

## Gotchas

- The kept-files-survive-branch-creation claim holds because `git checkout -b`/`createBranch` keeps the working tree; `freshRun`'s header commit is pathspec-scoped (`forceCommitOnly(store.path, ...)`, never `add -A`), so kept files reach the branch only via the first stage's own commit — this is already true for skip-branch and needs stating in the new scaladoc for normal mode.
- `snapshotLog`/`restoreLogIfMissing` bracket the cleanliness call — do not reorder anything around them.
- Live-test /tmp note: if runner tests all start failing with exit 1, /tmp is full of `orca-*` temp repos — clean them, it's not your change.
- Do not touch the shell's interactive menu prompt (`promptCreateBranch` in `Main.scala`) — keep-changes is CLI-flag-only in the shell; the runtime's own prompt covers the interactive case.
